title: Warnaar–Zudilin q-rious unimodality
source: S. Ole Warnaar and Wadim Zudilin, q-rious unimodality, arXiv:2502.03993v2, Conjecture 5 and equations (1),(2). https://arxiv.org/html/2502.03993v2
source_open_excerpt: Paraphrase: Landau's floor-function criterion for a factorial ratio is conjectured to imply unimodality after multiplying its q-analogue by 1+q.
source_paper_text: Operator editorial formalization. Let r,s>=1 and let a=(a_1,...,a_r), b=(b_1,...,b_s) be tuples of positive integers. Assume L(x)=sum_i floor(a_i*x)-sum_j floor(b_j*x)>=0 for EVERY real x>=0. Define [m]_q=1+q+...+q^(m-1), [m]_q!=product_{h=1}^m[h]_q, and [0]_q!=1. Put D(a,b;q)=product_i[a_i]_q! / product_j[b_j]_q!. Under the hypothesis D belongs to Z[q]. Conjecture 5: (1+q)D(a,b;q) is unimodal: writing its complete coefficient sequence c_0,...,c_d, some h satisfies c_0<=...<=c_h>=...>=c_d. Do not replace Landau's all-x criterion with mere polynomial divisibility. A refutation must certify the floor-function hypothesis for all x and display an exact nonunimodal coefficient sequence. The source proves selected families and reports finite checks; general validity is conjectural.
target: Settle the full original conjecture, prioritizing discovery of a finite counterexample. For REFUTED provide exact witness data, a proof that every hypothesis holds, and a reproducible exact certificate of the failed conclusion. Numerical approximations alone are insufficient. A valid universal proof is PROVED, not REFUTED; finite passing searches are only partial progress.
